_doc: 독일어 원문은 루트비히 놀이 엮은 『Mozarts Briefe』(잘츠부르크 1865, 공공 영역) 쪽 스캔을 직접 읽어 옮겼고, 판본의 철자(daß, Theil, -iren 등)와 문장부호를 그대로 두었다. 영어는 레이디 월리스의 1866년 번역(공공 영역)을 그대로 따랐다. 한국어는 이 앱이 새로 옮긴 것이다.

messages.de: Mich freut es recht von ganzem Herzen, daß Du bei der Schlittenfahrt, von der Du mir schreibst, Dich so sehr ergötzt hast, und ich wünsche Dir tausend Gelegenheiten zur Ergötzung, damit Du recht lustig Dein Leben zubringen mögtest.
messages.en: I rejoice in my heart that you were so well amused at the sledging party you write to me about, and I wish you a thousand opportunities of pleasure, so that you may pass your life merrily.
messages.ko: 누나가 편지에 쓴 썰매 타기가 그렇게 즐거웠다니 진심으로 기뻐. 누나한테 즐거울 일이 천 번은 더 생겨서, 평생 신나게 살면 좋겠어.
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 3 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

messages.de: Just ehe ich diesen Brief angefangen habe, habe ich eine Arie aus dem Demetrio [von Metastasio] verfertigt, welche so anfängt: Misero tu non sei etc.
messages.en: Just before beginning this letter I composed an air from the "Demetrio" of Metastasio, which begins thus, "Misero tu non sei."
messages.ko: 이 편지를 쓰기 바로 전에 메타스타시오의 〈데메트리오〉에 나오는 아리아를 하나 지었어. ‘미제로 투 논 세이’로 시작하는 거야.
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 3 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

messages.de: Die prima Donna singt gut, aber still; und wenn man sie nicht agiren sähe, sondern singen nur allein, so meynte man, sie sänge nicht, denn den Mund kann sie nicht öffnen, sondern winselt Alles her …
messages.en: The prima donna sings well, but is inanimate, and if you did not see her acting, but only singing, you might suppose she was not singing at all, for she can't open her mouth, and whines out everything.
messages.ko: 프리마 돈나는 노래는 잘하는데 힘이 없어. 연기하는 걸 안 보고 노래만 들으면 노래를 안 하는 줄 알 거야. 입을 못 벌리고 다 낑낑대듯 부르거든.
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 3 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

speak.en: The prima donna sings well, / but is inanimate, / and if you did not see her acting, / but only singing, / you might suppose she was not singing at all, / for she can't open her mouth, / and whines out everything.
speak.ko: 프리마 돈나는 노래는 잘하는데 힘이 없어. // 연기하는 걸 안 보고 노래만 들으면 노래를 안 하는 줄 알 거야. // 입을 못 벌리고 다 낑낑대듯 부르거든.

messages.de: Die seconda Donna macht ein Ansehen wie ein Grenadier, und hat auch eine starke Stimme; und singt wahrhaftig nicht übel, für das, daß sie das erste Mal agirt.
messages.en: The seconda donna looks like a grenadier, and has a very powerful voice; she really does not sing badly, considering that this is her first appearance.
messages.ko: 세콘다 돈나는 척탄병처럼 생겼고 목소리도 우렁차. 첫 무대인 걸 생각하면 정말 못 부르는 건 아니야.
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 3 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

messages.de: Ein Grotesco ist da, der gut springt, aber nicht so schreibt wie ich: wie die Säue brumzen.
messages.en: There is a grotesco who jumps cleverly, but cannot write as I do--just as pigs grunt.
messages.ko: 그로테스코 무용수가 하나 있는데 점프는 잘해. 그런데 나처럼은 못 써. 돼지가 꿀꿀대듯이 쓰거든.
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 3 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

note.ko: 그림은 1747년 밀라노 레조 두칼레 극장에서 열린 축하 무도회 장면이에요. 편지 속 만토바·크레모나의 극장은 아니지만, 바로 이 극장에서 그해 12월 볼프강의 오페라 〈미트리다테〉가 막을 올렸어요. 볼프강은 1769년 12월 아버지 레오폴트와 함께 첫 이탈리아 여행을 떠났어요. 이 편지는 열네 번째 생일 하루 전, 밀라노에서 썼어요. 만토바와 크레모나에서 본 오페라 가수들을 누나에게 장난스럽게 평가해요.
note.en: The picture shows a festival ball in Milan's Teatro Regio Ducale in 1747 — not the theatres of Mantua and Cremona in the letter, but the house where Wolfgang's opera 'Mitridate' opened that December. In December 1769 Wolfgang set off with his father Leopold on his first journey to Italy. He wrote this from Milan the day before his fourteenth birthday, giving his sister a mischievous review of the singers he had heard in Mantua and Cremona.
note.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 3 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

replies.de: Du hast eine neue Arie! Ich bin so stolz.
replies.en: You have a new aria again! I feel so proud.
replies.ko: 새 아리아가 또 하나 있어요! 정말 자랑스러워요.
replies.koLow: 새 아리아가 또 하나 있어! 정말 자랑스러워.
replies.koHigh: 새 아리아가 또 하나 있습니다! 정말 자랑스럽습니다.

why.ko: 편지 속 가수들은 만토바와 크레모나에서 노래했지만, 이 그림은 볼프강이 편지를 쓴 밀라노의 큰 오페라 극장이에요. 18세기 이탈리아 극장의 객석과 무대가 어땠는지 보여 줘요.
why.en: The singers in the letter performed in Mantua and Cremona, but this is the great opera house of Milan, where Wolfgang was writing. It shows what an 18th-century Italian theatre, with its tiers of boxes and its stage, looked like.

note.ko: 무대 안쪽 끝. 오페라 날이면 프리마 돈나가 여기 섰어요.
note.en: The far end is the stage, where on opera nights the prima donna stood.

note.ko: 오늘 밤 마루는 무도회장이에요. 볼프강이 놀린 그로테스코 무용수도 이런 무대에서 뛰었어요.
note.en: Tonight the floor is a ballroom. The grotesco dancer Wolfgang teases leapt on stages like this.

q.de: Was hat Wolfgang kurz vor dem Brief gemacht?
q.en: What did Wolfgang do just before writing this letter?
q.ko: 볼프강은 이 편지를 쓰기 바로 전에 뭘 했어요?

lines.de: Hallo Nannerl! Wie geht's dir?
lines.en: Hi Nannerl! How are you?

lines.de: Gut, danke! Ich bin gesund.
lines.en: Good, thanks! I'm well.

lines.de: Die Sängerin hat eine gute Stimme.
lines.en: The singer has a good voice.

lines.de: Schön! Schreib mir bald einen Brief!
lines.en: Nice! Write me a letter soon!

messages.de: Ich bin, Gott Lob und Dank! nebst meiner miserablen Feder gesund und küsse die Mama und die Nannerl tausend oder 1000 Mal.
messages.en: I am thankful to say that my stupid pen and I are all right, so we send a thousand kisses to you both.
messages.ko: 하느님 덕분에 저는 이 엉터리 펜이랑 같이 잘 있어요. 엄마와 누나에게 천 번, 아니 1000번 입맞춤을 보내요.
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 9 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

speak.de: Ich bin, / Gott Lob und Dank! // nebst meiner miserablen Feder gesund und küsse die Mama und die Nannerl tausend oder 1000 Mal.
speak.en: I am thankful to say that my stupid pen and I are all right, / so we send a thousand kisses to you both.
speak.ko: 하느님 덕분에 저는 이 엉터리 펜이랑 같이 잘 있어요. // 엄마와 누나에게 천 번, / 아니 1000번 입맞춤을 보내요.

messages.de: Ich wünschte nur, daß meine Schwester zu Rom wäre, denn ihr würde diese Stadt gewiß wohl gefallen, indem die Peterskirche regulär, und viele andere Sachen zu Rom regulär sind.
messages.en: I wish that my sister were in Rome, for this city would assuredly delight her, because St. Peter's is symmetrical, and many other things in Rome are also symmetrical.
messages.ko: 누나가 로마에 있으면 좋겠어요. 이 도시가 분명 마음에 들 거예요. 성 베드로 대성당이 반듯반듯하고, 로마의 다른 많은 것들도 반듯반듯하거든요.
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 9 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

speak.de: Ich wünschte nur, / daß meine Schwester zu Rom wäre, / denn ihr würde diese Stadt gewiß wohl gefallen, / indem die Peterskirche regulär, / und viele andere Sachen zu Rom regulär sind.
speak.en: I wish that my sister were in Rome, / for this city would assuredly delight her, / because St. Peter's is symmetrical, / and many other things in Rome are also symmetrical.
speak.ko: 누나가 로마에 있으면 좋겠어요. // 이 도시가 분명 마음에 들 거예요. // 성 베드로 대성당이 반듯반듯하고, / 로마의 다른 많은 것들도 반듯반듯하거든요.

messages.de: O ich habe eine Noth. In unserm Quartier ist nur ein Bett. Das kann die Mama sich leicht einbilden, daß ich bei dem Papa keine Ruhe habe.
messages.en: Oh! I have one annoyance--there is only a single bed in our lodgings, so mamma may easily imagine that I get no rest beside papa.
messages.ko: 아, 곤란한 게 하나 있어요. 우리 숙소엔 침대가 하나뿐이에요. 아빠 옆에서 제가 통 쉬지 못한다는 거, 엄마는 쉽게 짐작하시겠죠.
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 9 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

speak.de: O ich habe eine Noth. // In unserm Quartier ist nur ein Bett. // Das kann die Mama sich leicht einbilden, / daß ich bei dem Papa keine Ruhe habe.
speak.en: Oh! // I have one annoyance--there is only a single bed in our lodgings, / so mamma may easily imagine that I get no rest beside papa.
speak.ko: 아, / 곤란한 게 하나 있어요. // 우리 숙소엔 침대가 하나뿐이에요. // 아빠 옆에서 제가 통 쉬지 못한다는 거, / 엄마는 쉽게 짐작하시겠죠.

messages.de: Jetzt habe ich just den heil. Petrus mit dem Schlüsselamt, den heiligen Paulus mit dem Schwert, und den heiligen Lukas mit meiner Schwester etc. etc. abgezeichnet.
messages.en: I have just finished sketching St. Peter with his keys, St. Paul with his sword, and St. Luke with--my sister, &c., &c.
messages.ko: 방금 열쇠를 든 성 베드로, 칼을 든 성 바오로, 그리고 성 루카를… 누나랑 같이 그려 봤어요.
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 9 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

speak.de: Jetzt habe ich just den heil. Petrus mit dem Schlüsselamt, / den heiligen Paulus mit dem Schwert, / und den heiligen Lukas mit meiner Schwester etc. etc. abgezeichnet.
speak.en: I have just finished sketching St. Peter with his keys, / St. Paul with his sword, / and St. Luke with--my sister, / &c., / &c.
speak.ko: 방금 열쇠를 든 성 베드로, / 칼을 든 성 바오로, / 그리고 성 루카를… 누나랑 같이 그려 봤어요.

messages.de: Ich habe die Ehre gehabt, des heil. Petrus Fuß zu S. Pietro zu küssen, und weil ich das Unglück habe, so klein zu sein, so hat man mich als den nämlichen alten Wolfgang Mozart hinaufgehoben.
messages.en: I had the honor of kissing St. Peter's foot at San Pietro, and as I have the misfortune to be so short, your good old Wolfgang Mozart was lifted up!
messages.ko: 산 피에트로 성당에서 성 베드로 상의 발에 입 맞추는 영광을 누렸어요. 그런데 불행히도 제가 키가 너무 작아서, 이 변함없는 볼프강 모차르트를 누가 번쩍 들어 올려 줬어요.
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 9 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

speak.de: Ich habe die Ehre gehabt, / des heil. Petrus Fuß zu S. Pietro zu küssen, / und weil ich das Unglück habe, / so klein zu sein, / so hat man mich als den nämlichen alten Wolfgang Mozart hinaufgehoben.
speak.en: I had the honor of kissing St. Peter's foot at San Pietro, / and as I have the misfortune to be so short, / your good old Wolfgang Mozart was lifted up!
speak.ko: 산 피에트로 성당에서 성 베드로 상의 발에 입 맞추는 영광을 누렸어요. // 그런데 불행히도 제가 키가 너무 작아서, / 이 변함없는 볼프강 모차르트를 누가 번쩍 들어 올려 줬어요.

note.ko: 부자는 1770년 4월 로마에 머물렀어요. 이 무렵 볼프강은 시스티나 성당에서 알레그리의 〈미제레레〉를 듣고 기억만으로 악보에 옮겨 적은 것으로 유명해요. 이 짧은 글은 아버지 편지 끝에 붙인 추신이에요.
note.en: Father and son spent April 1770 in Rome. It was during these days that Wolfgang famously heard Allegri's Miserere in the Sistine Chapel and wrote it down from memory. This short text is a postscript added to his father's letter.
note.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 9 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

replies.de: Rom ist sicher schön. Ich bin ganz neidisch!
replies.en: Rome sounds lovely. I feel quite jealous!

why.ko: 볼프강이 누나에게 ‘반듯반듯하다’고 자랑한 성 베드로 대성당을, 같은 세기 피라네시가 동판에 새긴 모습이에요.
why.en: St. Peter's, which Wolfgang praised to his sister as 'symmetrical', etched by Piranesi in the same century.

note.ko: 미켈란젤로가 설계한 큰 돔.
note.en: The great dome designed by Michelangelo.

note.ko: 광장을 양팔처럼 감싸는 열주랑이 좌우로 똑같아요. 볼프강이 말한 ‘반듯함’이에요.
note.en: The colonnades embrace the square like two matching arms — the symmetry Wolfgang liked.

note.ko: 이 문 안쪽에 성 베드로 청동상이 있어요. 키 작은 볼프강은 들어 올려져 그 발에 입 맞췄지요.
note.en: Inside these doors stands the bronze St. Peter; little Wolfgang had to be lifted up to kiss its foot.

q.de: Warum kann Wolfgang nicht gut schlafen?
q.en: Why can't Wolfgang get any rest?

messages.de: Der 12te Menuett von Haydn, den Du mir geschickt hast, gefällt mir recht wohl, und den Baß hast du unvergleichlich dazu componirt, und ohne mindesten Fehler.
messages.en: Haydn's twelfth minuet, which you sent me, pleases me very much; you have composed an inimitable bass for it, and without the slightest fault.

messages.de: Schreibe mir, wie es dem Herrn Canari geht. Singt er noch? Pfeift er noch?
messages.en: Tell me how Master Canary is? Does he still sing? and still whistle?
messages.ko: 카나리아 나리는 어떻게 지내는지 알려 줘. 아직 노래해? 아직 휘파람 불어?

speak.de: Schreibe mir, / wie es dem Herrn Canari geht. // Singt er noch? // Pfeift er noch?

messages.de: Weißt Du, warum ich auf den Canari denke? Weil in unserm Vorzimmer einer ist, welcher ein G'seis macht, wie unserer.
messages.en: Do you know why I am thinking about the canary? Because we have one in our ante-room that chirps out a G sharp just like ours.
messages.ko: 내가 왜 카나리아 생각을 하는지 알아? 여기 우리 곁방에도 한 마리 있는데, 우리 애처럼 올림 솔 소리를 내거든.
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 12 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

messages.de: Gestern haben wir unsere neuen Kleider angezogen; wir waren schön wie die Engel.
messages.en: Yesterday we wore our new clothes; we were as handsome as angels.
messages.ko: 어제 새 옷을 입었어. 우리 둘 다 천사처럼 멋졌지.

messages.de: Die Königin und den König haben wir unter der Messe zu Portici in der Hofcapelle gesehen, und den Vesuvius haben wir auch gesehen. Neapel ist schön, ist aber volkreich wie Wien und Paris.
messages.en: We saw the king and queen at mass in the court chapel at Portici, and we also saw Vesuvius. Naples is beautiful, but as crowded with people as Vienna or Paris.
messages.ko: 포르티치 궁정 예배당 미사에서 왕비와 왕을 봤고, 베수비오 화산도 봤어. 나폴리는 아름다운데, 빈이나 파리처럼 사람이 북적여.
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 12 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

speak.de: Die Königin und den König haben wir unter der Messe zu Portici in der Hofcapelle gesehen, / und den Vesuvius haben wir auch gesehen. // Neapel ist schön, / ist aber volkreich wie Wien und Paris.
speak.en: We saw the king and queen at mass in the court chapel at Portici, / and we also saw Vesuvius. // Naples is beautiful, / but as crowded with people as Vienna or Paris.
speak.ko: 포르티치 궁정 예배당 미사에서 왕비와 왕을 봤고, / 베수비오 화산도 봤어. // 나폴리는 아름다운데, / 빈이나 파리처럼 사람이 북적여.

note.ko: 그림은 볼프강이 본 바로 그날이 아니라, 같은 시절 베수비오 화산의 분화를 그린 1777년 그림이에요. 편지 첫머리는 이탈리아어로, 연습 삼아 썼어요. 나폴리 왕 부부를 본 포르티치는 베수비오 화산 기슭의 왕궁이 있는 곳이에요. 이 편지를 엮은 놀은 모차르트가 동물을 무척 좋아해 나중에도 늘 방에 새를 두었다고 적었어요.
note.en: A painting of Vesuvius erupting from the same years (1777), not the day Wolfgang saw it. The opening of the letter is written in Italian, as practice. Portici, where he saw the royal couple, is the site of a royal palace at the foot of Vesuvius. Nohl, who edited the letters, notes that Mozart loved animals and later always kept birds in his room.
note.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 12 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

replies.de: Danke für dein Lob! Ich bin heute sehr glücklich.
replies.en: Thanks for your praise! I feel very happy today.

text.de: Mozart liebte die Thiere sehr und hatte auch später stets Vögel im Zimmer.
text.en: Mozart loved animals and later always kept birds in his room.
text.ko: 모차르트는 동물을 무척 좋아해, 나중에도 늘 방에 새를 두었어요.

caption.en: Ferdinand IV, King of Naples, as a boy

why.ko: 볼프강이 나폴리에서 ‘베수비오도 봤다’고 쓴 그 화산이에요. 나폴리에 살던 프랑스 화가 볼레르가 몇 해 뒤 그린 밤의 분화 장면이에요.
why.en: The volcano Wolfgang says he saw from Naples, painted a few years later by Volaire, a French painter working in Naples, erupting by night.

note.ko: 불을 뿜는 화산 꼭대기. 용암이 산비탈로 흘러내려요.
note.en: The burning summit, with lava pouring down its slopes.

note.ko: 달빛 아래 나폴리 만. 볼프강이 ‘아름답다’고 한 도시가 이 바닷가에 있어요.
note.en: The moonlit Bay of Naples; the city Wolfgang called beautiful lies along this shore.

note.ko: 멋지게 차려입은 구경꾼들. 볼프강 부자도 새 옷을 입고 나폴리를 다녔어요.
note.en: Smartly dressed sightseers; father and son, too, went about Naples in new clothes.

q.de: Nach wem fragt Wolfgang zu Hause?
q.en: Who at home does Wolfgang ask about?
q.ko: 볼프강은 집에 있는 누구의 안부를 물어요?

scene.ko: 나폴리의 볼프강과 통화 · 나는 누나 난네를
scene.en: A call with Wolfgang in Naples · I'm his sister Nannerl

lines.de: Nannerl, dein Bass hat keinen Fehler!
lines.en: Nannerl, your bass has no mistakes!

lines.de: Danke! Wie ist Neapel?
lines.en: Thanks! What's Naples like?

lines.de: Schön! Und wir haben neue Kleider!
lines.en: Lovely! And we have new clothes!

lines.de: Toll! Aber ich sehe sie nicht.
lines.en: Great! But I can't see them.

messages.de: Ich kann ohnmöglich schöner schreiben, denn die Feder ist eine Notenfeder und keine Schriftfeder.
messages.en: I can't possibly write better, for my pen is only fit to write music and not a letter.
messages.ko: 글씨를 더 예쁘게 쓰는 건 도저히 못 하겠어. 이 펜은 악보 펜이지 편지 펜이 아니거든.

messages.de: Nun ist meine Geige neu beseitet und ich spiele alle Tage; aber dieses setze ich nur hinzu, weil meine Mama einmal zu wissen verlangte, ob ich noch geige.
messages.en: My violin has been newly strung, and I play every day. I only mention this because mamma wished to know whether I still played the violin.
messages.ko: 이제 내 바이올린에 줄을 새로 매어서 매일 켜. 이건 엄마가 내가 아직 바이올린을 켜는지 알고 싶어 하셔서 덧붙이는 거야.

messages.de: Gewiß ihrer 6 mal habe ich die Ehre gehabt, allein in die Kirchen und prächtige Functiones zu gehen.
messages.en: I have had the honor to go at least six times by myself into the churches to attend their splendid ceremonies.
messages.ko: 적어도 여섯 번은 혼자서 성당에 가서 화려한 예식을 보는 영광을 누렸어.

messages.de: Unterdessen habe ich schon vier italienische Sinfonien [Ouvertüren] componirt, außer den Arien, deren ich gewiß 5—6 schon gemacht habe, und auch eine Motetten.
messages.en: In the mean time I have composed four Italian symphonies [overtures], besides five or six arias, and also a motett.
messages.ko: 그동안 이탈리아식 신포니아를 벌써 네 곡 지었어. 아리아도 대여섯 곡 썼고, 모테트도 하나 썼어.

speak.en: In the mean time I have composed four Italian symphonies [overtures], / besides five or six arias, / and also a motett.

messages.de: Addio! Lebe wohl, meine einzige Lustbarkeit besteht dermalen in englischen Schritten, Capriol- und Spaggat-machen. Italien ist ein Schlafland; es schläfert Einen immer.
messages.en: Addio--farewell! My sole recreations consist in dancing English hornpipes and cutting capers. Italy is a land of sleep; I am always drowsy here.
messages.ko: 안녕, 잘 지내. 요즘 내 유일한 낙은 영국식 춤 스텝 밟고 깡충 뛰고 다리 찢기 하는 거야. 이탈리아는 잠의 나라야. 늘 졸려.
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 19 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

speak.en: Addio--farewell! // My sole recreations consist in dancing English hornpipes and cutting capers. // Italy is a land of sleep; // I am always drowsy here.

note.ko: 그림은 마르티니 신부를 1776년에 새긴 판화예요. 신부는 편지에 나오지 않지만, 볼로냐에서 볼프강을 가르친 사람이에요. 한여름 볼로냐에서 아버지 편지에 덧붙인 추신이에요. 그해 10월 볼프강은 볼로냐의 아카데미아 필라르모니카에 회원으로 받아들여졌어요. 마르티니 신부가 이끌던 이 도시는 이탈리아 음악 학문의 중심지였어요.
note.en: The picture is a 1776 engraving of Padre Martini. He is not named in the letter, but he taught Wolfgang in Bologna. A postscript to his father's letter, written in the summer heat of Bologna. That October Wolfgang was admitted to Bologna's Accademia Filarmonica. The city, home of Padre Martini, was a centre of musical learning in Italy.
note.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 19 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

replies.de: Das wollte ich auch wissen! Was spielst du gerade?

why.ko: 편지가 쓰인 볼로냐의 음악 학자 마르티니 신부를 새긴 판화예요. 볼프강은 이 무렵 볼로냐에서 그에게 대위법을 배웠어요.
why.en: An engraved portrait of Padre Martini, the music scholar of Bologna, where this letter was written; Wolfgang studied counterpoint with him there at this time.

note.ko: 아래 글귀에는 그가 1725년 볼로냐 산프란체스코 성당의 악장이 되었다고 적혀 있어요. 성당 음악을 짓는 사람이었지요.
note.en: The caption says he was made maestro di cappella of the church of San Francesco in Bologna in 1725 — a composer of church music.

note.ko: 수도복과 두건. 글귀대로 그는 1721년 프란치스코회 수도복을 입었어요. 볼프강도 혼자 성당 예식을 보러 다녔지요.
note.en: Habit and cap: as the caption says, he took the Franciscan habit in 1721. Wolfgang, too, went to the church ceremonies on his own.

lines.de: Hallo Nannerl! Hier ist Wolfgang!
lines.en: Hi Nannerl! It's Wolfgang here!

lines.de: Hallo! Spielst du noch Geige?
lines.en: Hi! Do you still play violin?

lines.de: Ja, jeden Tag! Mit neuen Saiten.
lines.en: Yes, every day! With new strings.

lines.de: Super! Aber du bist müde, oder?
lines.en: Great! But you're tired, aren't you?

messages.de: Wir haben auf der Reise viele Hitz ausgestanden, und der Staub hat uns beständig impertinent seckirt, daß wir gewiß erstickt und verschmachtet wären, wenn wir nicht gescheiter gewesen wären.
messages.en: We suffered much from heat in the course of our journey, and the dust constantly dried us up so impertinently that we should have been choked, or died of thirst, if we had not been too sensible for that.
messages.ko: 오는 길에 더위를 엄청 견뎠어. 먼지가 어찌나 뻔뻔하게 괴롭히던지, 우리가 좀 더 똑똑하지 않았으면 숨 막히고 목말라 죽었을 거야.
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 33 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

speak.en: We suffered much from heat in the course of our journey, / and the dust constantly dried us up so impertinently that we should have been choked, / or died of thirst, / if we had not been too sensible for that.

messages.de: Hier hat es ein ganzes Monath durch (sagen die Mayländer) nicht gerenget, heunt hat es angefangen ein wenig zu tröpfeln, jetzt aber scheunt wieder die Sonne und es ist wieder sehr warm.
messages.en: For a whole month past (say the Milanese) there has been no rain here; to-day a slight drizzle began, but the sun has now come out again, and it is once more very warm.
messages.ko: 여기는 (밀라노 사람들 말로는) 한 달 내내 비가 안 왔대. 오늘 빗방울이 조금 떨어지기 시작했는데, 지금은 다시 해가 나서 또 아주 더워.
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 33 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

messages.de: Jetzt blas ich just vor Hitz! Nun reiß ich das Leibel auf.
messages.en: I am at this moment actually panting from the heat--I tear open my waistcoat!
messages.ko: 지금 더워서 헉헉대는 중이야! 이제 조끼를 확 풀어 젖힌다.

messages.en: Above us we have a violinist, below us is another, next to us a singing-master, who gives lessons, and, in the room opposite, a hautboy-player.

messages.de: Das ist lustig zum Componiren! Giebt einen viel Gedanken.

note.ko: 그림은 이 편지와 직접 관계없는, 음악을 연주하는 아이들을 그린 옛 판화예요. 1771년 3월 말 잘츠부르크로 돌아왔던 부자는 몇 달 만에 다시 밀라노로 떠났어요. 마리아 테레지아 여제가 페르디난트 대공과 모데나 공녀의 10월 결혼식을 위한 세레나타를 볼프강에게 맡겼기 때문이에요. 그 작품이 〈알바의 아스카니오〉예요.
note.en: The picture is an old print of children making music, not directly connected with this letter. Father and son had come home to Salzburg at the end of March 1771, but left for Milan again a few months later. Empress Maria Theresa had commissioned from Wolfgang a theatrical serenata for the October wedding of Archduke Ferdinand and the Princess of Modena: 'Ascanio in Alba'.
note.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 33 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

replies.de: Überall Musiker! Ich liebe das auch. Wer spielt am besten?
replies.en: Musicians everywhere! You love it, so do I. Who's best?
replies.ko: 온통 음악가예요! 저도 그런 곳이 좋아요. 누가 제일 잘해요?
replies.koLow: 온통 음악가야! 나도 그런 곳이 좋아. 누가 제일 잘해?
replies.koHigh: 온통 음악가입니다! 저도 그런 곳이 좋습니다. 누가 제일 잘합니까?

moments.quote: jetzt aber scheunt wieder die Sonne

text.de: Ein Monat ohne Regen, dann wieder Sonne
text.en: A month without rain, then sun again
text.ko: 한 달 동안 비 없음, 다시 쨍쨍

caption.en: Milan: San Babila and Santa Marta, c. 1745

why.ko: 위아래 옆방에서 바이올린, 노래, 오보에 소리가 들려오던 밀라노 숙소처럼, 아이들이 저마다 피리를 불고 노래하는 옛 판화예요.
why.en: An old print of children each piping or singing at once — like the Milan lodging, with music coming from every room around.

note.ko: 관악기를 부는 아이. 맞은편 방의 오보에 주자 같아요.
note.en: A child blowing a reed pipe, like the oboist across the landing.

note.ko: 입을 벌리고 노래하는 아이. 옆방 성악 선생의 레슨 같아요.
note.en: A child singing with mouth wide open — like the singing-master's lesson next door.

note.ko: 펼친 악보책. 시끄러운 숙소가 오히려 ‘작곡하기에 딱’이라고 했지요.
note.en: An open music book; Wolfgang said the noisy house was just the place for composing.

scene.ko: 더운 밀라노에 막 도착한 볼프강과 통화 · 나는 누나 난네를
scene.en: A call with Wolfgang, just arrived in hot Milan · I'm his sister Nannerl

lines.de: Hallo Nannerl! Hier ist es heiß!
lines.en: Hi Nannerl! It's hot here!

lines.de: Wie geht's nach der Reise?
lines.en: How are you after the journey?

lines.de: Seit einem Monat gibt's keinen Regen!
lines.en: No rain for a whole month!

lines.de: Und dein Zimmer? Ist es ruhig?
lines.en: And your room? Is it quiet?

letters.ref: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 48 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

messages.de: Ich hoffe Du wirst Dich gut befinden meine liebe Schwester.
messages.en: I hope, dear sister, that you are well, dear sister.
messages.ko: 잘 지내고 있겠지, 사랑하는 누나.
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 48 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

speak.de: Ich hoffe Du wirst Dich gut befinden meine liebe Schwester.
speak.en: I hope, / dear sister, / that you are well, / dear sister.
speak.ko: 잘 지내고 있겠지, / 사랑하는 누나.

messages.de: Wenn Du diesen Brief erhaltst meine liebe Schwester, so geht denselbigen Abend meine liebe Schwester meine Opera in scena.
messages.en: When this letter reaches you, dear sister, my opera will be in scena, dear sister.
messages.ko: 이 편지를 받을 때쯤이면, 사랑하는 누나, 바로 그날 저녁에, 사랑하는 누나, 내 오페라가 무대에 올라.
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 48 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

speak.de: Wenn Du diesen Brief erhaltst meine liebe Schwester, / so geht denselbigen Abend meine liebe Schwester meine Opera in scena.
speak.en: When this letter reaches you, / dear sister, / my opera will be in scena, / dear sister.

messages.de: Denke auf mich meine liebe Schwester und bilde dir nur meine liebe Schwester kräftig ein, Du siehest und hörest meine liebe Schwester sie auch.
messages.en: Think of me, dear sister, and try, dear sister, to imagine with all your might that my dear sister sees and hears it also.
messages.ko: 나를 생각해 줘, 사랑하는 누나. 그리고 힘껏 상상해 봐, 사랑하는 누나. 사랑하는 누나도 그걸 보고 듣고 있다고.
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 48 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

speak.de: Denke auf mich meine liebe Schwester und bilde dir nur meine liebe Schwester kräftig ein, / Du siehest und hörest meine liebe Schwester sie auch.
speak.en: Think of me, / dear sister, / and try, / dear sister, / to imagine with all your might that my dear sister sees and hears it also.

messages.de: Die morgige Probe ist auf dem Theatro. Der Impressario aber der Sig. Cassiglioni hat mich ersucht, ich solle niemand nichts darvon sagen, denn sonst lauffen alle Leute hinein, und das wollen wir nicht.
messages.en: The rehearsal to-morrow is to be in the theatre. The impresario, Signor Cassiglioni, has entreated me not to say a word of this to a soul, as all kinds of people would come crowding in, and that we don't wish.
messages.ko: 내일 리허설은 극장에서 해. 그런데 극장주 카스틸리오니 씨가 아무한테도 말하지 말라고 부탁했어. 안 그러면 사람들이 다 몰려들 텐데, 우린 그건 싫거든.
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 48 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

speak.de: Die morgige Probe ist auf dem Theatro. // Der Impressario aber der Sig. Cassiglioni hat mich ersucht, / ich solle niemand nichts darvon sagen, / denn sonst lauffen alle Leute hinein, / und das wollen wir nicht.
speak.en: The rehearsal to-morrow is to be in the theatre. // The impresario, / Signor Cassiglioni, / has entreated me not to say a word of this to a soul, / as all kinds of people would come crowding in, / and that we don't wish.

messages.de: Wir giengen heunt von Graf Firmian weck um nach Haus zu gehen, und als wir in unser Gassen kommen, so machten wir unser Hausthüre auf, und was meinste wohl was sich zugetragen? — Wir giengen hinein.
messages.en: We were going home straight from Count Firmiani's, and when we came into our street we opened our door, and what do you think happened? We went in.
messages.ko: 오늘 피르미안 백작 댁에서 나와 집으로 가는데, 우리 골목에 들어서서 현관문을 열었어. 그랬더니 무슨 일이 벌어졌게? — 우리가 안으로 들어갔지.
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 48 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

speak.de: Wir giengen heunt von Graf Firmian weck um nach Haus zu gehen, / und als wir in unser Gassen kommen, / so machten wir unser Hausthüre auf, / und was meinste wohl was sich zugetragen? // — / Wir giengen hinein.
speak.en: We were going home straight from Count Firmiani's, / and when we came into our street we opened our door, / and what do you think happened? // We went in.
speak.ko: 오늘 피르미안 백작 댁에서 나와 집으로 가는데, / 우리 골목에 들어서서 현관문을 열었어. // 그랬더니 무슨 일이 벌어졌게? // — / 우리가 안으로 들어갔지.

note.ko: 세 번째 이탈리아 여행에서 볼프강은 밀라노를 위해 오페라 〈루치오 실라〉를 썼어요. 놀에 따르면 볼프강은 이 편지를 한 줄 쓸 때마다 종이를 뒤집어, 한 줄 걸러 한 줄씩 거꾸로 서 있어요. 오페라는 12월 26일 막을 올려 큰 성공을 거두고 날마다 극장을 채웠어요.
note.en: On his third Italian journey Wolfgang wrote the opera 'Lucio Silla' for Milan. Nohl reports that he turned the sheet round after every line, so every other line of this letter stands on its head. The opera opened on 26 December with great success and filled the house night after night.
note.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 48 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

replies.de: Ich bin nicht in Mailand, aber ich höre deine Oper.
replies.en: Do you know I hear your opera, far from Milan?
replies.ko: 밀라노엔 못 가요. 그래도 마음으로 오페라를 들어요.
replies.koLow: 밀라노엔 못 가. 그래도 마음으로 오페라를 들어.
replies.koHigh: 밀라노에는 못 갑니다. 그래도 마음으로 오페라를 듣습니다.

text.de: Jede zweite Zeile steht auf dem Kopfe.
text.en: Every other line is written upside down.
text.ko: 한 줄 걸러 한 줄씩 거꾸로 쓴 편지예요.

why.ko: 편지에서 볼프강이 ‘그날 저녁 무대에 오른다’고 한 바로 그 오페라의 인쇄 대본이에요. 레조 두칼 극장, 1773년 카니발 시즌이라고 적혀 있어요.
why.en: The printed libretto of the very opera Wolfgang says will be 'in scena' that evening, for the Regio Ducal Teatro in the Carnival season of 1773.

note.ko: ‘루치오 실라, 음악극’. 볼프강의 오페라 제목이에요.
note.en: 'Lucio Silla, dramma per musica' — the title of Wolfgang's opera.

note.ko: ‘밀라노 레조 두칼 극장에서 상연’. 리허설도 이 극장에서 했어요.
note.en: 'To be performed in the Regio Ducal Teatro of Milan' — where the rehearsal took place too.

q.de: Was passiert, wenn der Brief bei Nannerl ankommt?
q.en: What will be happening when the letter reaches Nannerl?
q.ko: 편지가 난네를에게 도착할 때쯤 무슨 일이 있어요?

options.de: Seine Oper ist auf der Bühne
options.en: His opera will be on stage

scene.ko: 오페라 첫 공연을 앞둔 볼프강과 통화 · 나는 누나 난네를
scene.en: A call with Wolfgang before his opera opens · I'm his sister Nannerl

lines.de: Nannerl, ich hoffe, dir geht's gut.
lines.en: Nannerl, I hope you're well.

lines.de: Ja, danke! Wann ist deine Oper?
lines.en: Yes, thanks! When is your opera?

lines.de: Morgen ist Probe. Sag's nicht weiter!
lines.en: Rehearsal's tomorrow. Don't tell anyone!

lines.de: Keine Sorge, ich sage nichts!
lines.en: Don't worry, I won't tell!
lines.ko: 걱정 마, 아무 말 안 할게!
